explanation: French cites Alford only for four-corners intent and harmonizing all parts of a deed; Luckel overruled Alford's granting-clause-controls holding and itself endorses the four-corners/harmonizing rule, so the negation is on a different point.

Second Circuit cites Lee for ordinary emotional or financial tribulations of family separation not being extreme hardship; Wang overruled Lee only insofar as inconsistent (prima facie showing, combined hardships) and itself says economic detriment alone is insufficient.

District court quotes Hammer as authority that the Tenth Amendment reserves local matters from Congress and strikes down a federal statute; Darby overruled Hammer and rejected that reasoning in 1941; no mention of Darby or the overruling.

Woods cites Walton II for abuse-of-discretion review of leave to amend; the 2007 Supreme Court decision reversed the later trial judgment on law-of-the-case grounds, not Walton II or its amendment standard, per the excerpt.

Betts appears only in Judge Wellford's separate opinion, as the source Screws quoted on due process being a fluid concept; it is description of Screws, not reliance on Betts's right-to-counsel holding that Gideon overruled.

Whitney appears only inside a block quotation from New York Times v. Sullivan citing Brandeis's concurrence on free discussion; Brandenburg overruled the Whitney majority's syndicalism holding, not that concurrence, and the court relies on Sullivan.

Valleylab cites Ex parte Slade in a string cite for the mandamus prerequisites; Creel overruled only Slade's portion on probate-court jurisdiction over common-law marriage and itself restates the same mandamus standard.
